summary: Where things are is said with a place word AFTER the noun — like a postposition: 桌子上 ‘on the table’ (table-top), 椅子下面 ‘under the chair’, 冰箱里 ‘in the fridge’, 沙发旁边 ‘next to the sofa’, 房子后面 ‘behind the house’, 床和衣柜中间 ‘between the bed and the wardrobe’. The whole frame is 在 + noun + place word: 书在桌子上. Short forms 上 / 下 / 里 attach to a noun; the long forms 上面, 下面, 里面, 外面, 前面, 后面, 旁边, 中间, 左边, 右边 can also stand alone (他在外面, 车站在前面). ‘There is X on Y’ turns round and starts with the place: 桌子上有一本书. Near and far are adjectives with 离 ‘from’: 超市离我家很近.

blocks.caption: 在 for known things, 有 for new things

blocks.title: Things become places with a place word
blocks.text: A place noun stands alone after 在: 在学校, 在北京, 在家. A thing needs a place word: 在冰箱里, 在桌子上 — *在冰箱 is incomplete. Rooms can go either way: 在厨房 / 在厨房里.

blocks.title: After the noun, not before
blocks.text: Greek πάνω στο τραπέζι, German auf dem Tisch put ‘on’ first. Chinese: 在桌子上 — *在上桌子 is wrong. Turkish works like Chinese: masanın üstünde ‘table-of top-at’.

items.title: Short: 上, 下, 里
points: 桌子上, 床下, 冰箱里

items.title: Long: 上面, 里面, 外面, 前面, 旁边 …
points: 桌子上面, 冰箱里面
书在上面 ✓, 他在外面 ✓

blocks.title: Near and far are adjectives
blocks.text: 近 and 远 work like adjectives, with 很: 很近, 很远. The point you measure from comes with 离: 超市离我家很近 ‘the supermarket is close to my home’; question: 远不远？ / 远吗？; ‘nearby’ is the noun 附近: 我家附近有一个公园.

blocks.title: On the floor, in the street, in the square
blocks.text: Surfaces take 上 even when they are not ‘on top’: 在地板上 ‘on the floor’, 在街上 ‘in the street’, 在广场上 ‘in the square’, 墙上 ‘on the wall’.

askYourself: Is the noun a place by itself (school, home, Beijing) or a thing (table, fridge, sofa)? → a thing needs a place word after it.
Which relation? on → 上, under → 下面, in → 里, outside → 外面, in front → 前面, behind → 后面, next to → 旁边, between → A 和 B 中间, left / right → 左边 / 右边.
Does the place word stand alone, without a noun? → use the long form: 在上面, 在里面, 在外面.
Is the thing known (the book) → thing + 在 + place; or new (a book) → place + 有 + thing?
Near or far? → A 离 B 很近 / 很远.
Is it a surface (floor, street, wall)? → 上.
Did I put the place word before the noun, like a preposition? → move it after the noun.
steps: 在 + the reference noun + the place word.
Or start with the place and use 有 for something new.

traps: *书在上桌子 → 书在桌子上.
*牛奶在冰箱 → 牛奶在冰箱里.
*书在上 → 书在上面 (a short form cannot stand alone).
*有一本书在桌子上 (copying English) → 桌子上有一本书.
*超市近我家 → 超市离我家很近.
*中间床和衣柜 → 床和衣柜中间.
‘Floor’ as a storey is not 地板: 三楼 ‘the third floor’.

quiz.why: 在 + noun + place word: the place word follows the noun.
A thing needs 里 to become a place.

quiz.q: ‘There is a sofa in the living room.’

quiz.why: Alone, the long form 外面 is used.

quiz.q: ‘The supermarket is very close to my home.’
quiz.why: Distance: A 离 B 很近.

quiz.q: ‘The table is between the bed and the wardrobe.’
quiz.why: Both sides first, then 中间.

quiz.q: Which language puts the place word after the noun, like Chinese?
quiz.why: Turkish, like Chinese, says ‘table top-at’; German and Greek put the preposition first.

seeAlso.note: German puts the preposition first and uses the dative for ‘where’ (auf dem Tisch, unter dem Stuhl, neben dem Sofa, zwischen dem Bett und dem Schrank); Chinese puts the place word after the noun and changes no ending.
German two-way prepositions switch case (Wo? auf dem Tisch / Wohin? auf den Tisch); Chinese keeps 在 … 上 for ‘where’ and uses a verb for ‘where to’.
Arabic places the word before the noun, which goes into the genitive: ʿalā, taḥta, bi-jānibi, amāma, khalfa / warāʾa, bayna.
Hebrew, too, puts it first: עַל, מִתַּחַת לְ־, לְיַד, לִפְנֵי, מֵאֲחוֹרֵי, בֵּין — Chinese turns the order round: 桌子上, 沙发旁边.
